transcript.text: t/d keeps cutting out after 10 mins then starts again if i leave it. vent hose goes out the window. pls help

This behaviour usually means the dryer is overheating and tripping a safety thermostat to cool down. The most common cause is restricted airflow (a full filter or blocked vent), though a faulty thermostat can also be the culprit. Please switch off and unplug the machine first. Then:
1) Clean the main fluff filter in the door opening (and any secondary filter at the bottom if your model has one).
2) Check the vent hose going out of the window is not kinked, crushed or blocked with lint. Let me know if these were clear and clean.
[Safety panel] Overheating can be a fire risk. Clean the lint filter and make sure the airflow/vent isn't blocked, and don't leave the dryer running unattended. If it smells of burning, stop using it and unplug it.

ok filter gets cleaned every time. just checked the hose and its crushed behind the dryer, i pushed it back further recently. theres fluff in the folds too. also the cabinet gets really hot before it stops

Please straighten the hose so it isn't squashed, clear out all the fluff from the folds, and make sure it has a gentle curve rather than a sharp bend. Once that is done, plug the dryer back in and run a test cycle. Does it now run for more than 10 minutes without cutting out? If you can also let me know the brand and model number (usually on a sticker inside the door opening), I can check if there are any specific recalls or known issues.
[Safety panel] Overheating can be a fire risk. Clean the lint filter and make sure the airflow/vent isn't blocked, and don't leave the dryer running unattended. If it smells of burning, stop using it and unplug it.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
its an Indesit, label inside the door says IDV 75. will straighten the hose and try a cycle

That crushed hose is almost certainly why it's overheating. Please straighten the hose so it isn't squashed, clear out all the fluff from the folds, and make sure it has a gentle curve rather than a sharp bend. Once that is done, plug the dryer back in and run a test cycle. Does it now run for more than 10 minutes without cutting out? If you can also let me know the brand and model number (usually on a sticker inside the door opening), I can check if there are any specific recalls or known issues.
[Safety panel] Overheating can be a fire risk. Clean the lint filter and make sure the airflow/vent isn't blocked, and don't leave the dryer running unattended. If it smells of burning, stop using it and unplug it.
ok hose straightened and fluff cleared, running a cycle now. what should i look out for?

Look out for two things: first, whether it completes the cycle (or at least runs much longer than 10 minutes) with the hose fixed. Second, check if the drum is spinning normally while it heats; if it stops spinning or moves very slowly, that points to a belt or motor issue rather than just overheating. Also, please check the condenser unit behind the bottom flap (if your model has one). If it's clogged with fluff, rinse it under the tap and let it drip-dry before putting it back. A blocked condenser will cause the same overheating cut-out as a blocked hose.
[Safety panel] Overheating can be a fire risk. Clean the lint filter and make sure the airflow/vent isn't blocked, and don't leave the dryer running unattended. If it smells of burning, stop using it and unplug it.
drum is spinning fine. not sure about a condenser, its a vented one with the hose out the window. will see if it gets past 10 mins

The crushed hose with fluff in the folds was almost certainly the cause. Please let me know if the cycle now runs for more than 10 minutes without cutting out after you straightened and cleared the hose. If it still cuts out after 10 minutes, we will need to check if there is a blockage further down the internal ducting or if the thermal cut-out has failed.
[Safety panel] Overheating can be a fire risk. Clean the lint filter and make sure the airflow/vent isn't blocked, and don't leave the dryer running unattended. If it smells of burning, stop using it and unplug it.
its been running a while now and still going, past 10 mins. will let you know if it stops

That is excellent news. The crushed hose was most likely causing the blockage that made the dryer overheat and cut out. To stop this happening again, just try to keep the hose straight when you push the machine back into place so it doesn't get squashed behind it again. If it starts doing it again in the future, check the filter and hose first. Is there anything else I can help with today?
